skills.name: Joint and partial variation, and variation graphs

note.text:
Joint variation: one quantity varies as two or more others together.
• z varies jointly as x and y: z = kxy.
• z varies directly as x and inversely as y: z = kx ÷ y.
Find k from one set of values, then use the formula.
Graphs: y = kx is a straight line through the origin; y = k ÷ x is a curve (hyperbola) that never meets the axes; y = kx² is a parabola through the origin.
Effect of changes: if y ∝ x², multiplying x by n multiplies y by n².

sections.heading: More than one cause
sections.text:
The cost of fuel for a trip depends on the distance and on the price per litre. Double either one and the cost doubles. We say the cost varies jointly as distance and price: C = kdp.
Joint variation multiplies the quantities. When one quantity varies inversely, it goes on the bottom: z varies directly as x and inversely as y means z = kx ÷ y.

sections.heading: Finding k and using it
sections.text:
z varies jointly as x and y, and z = {24} when x = {2} and y = {4}.
{24} = k × {2} × {4} = {mono(8, 'k')}, so k = {3} and z = {mono(3, 'xy')}.
When x = {5} and y = {2}: z = {3} × {5} × {2} = {30}.
The method is always: write the formula with k, find k, then use the formula.

sections.heading: Pictures of variation
sections.text:
• y = kx: a straight line through the origin. Equal steps in x give equal steps in y.
• y = k ÷ x: a curve. As x gets bigger, y gets smaller, but it never reaches zero.
• y = kx²: a U-shaped curve, the parabola. If x doubles, y becomes four times as big.
Reading a graph tells you which type of variation the data follow.

key_words.meaning: one quantity varies as the product of others: z = kxy
the curve of y = k ÷ x
the U-shaped curve of y = kx²

examples: Area of a rectangle varies jointly as its length and width (k = {1}).

mistake.wrong: z varies jointly as x and y: z = k(x + y)
mistake.why: Jointly means the quantities are multiplied together, not added.

worked_example.problem: z varies jointly as x and y. z = {k * x * y} when x = {x} and y = {y}. Find z when x = {X} and y = {Y}.

cards.idea: Jointly as x and y: z = kxy.
Directly as x and inversely as y: z = kx ÷ y.
The graph of y = kx is a straight line through the origin; y = k ÷ x is a curve.
example: Doubling x doubles y on the line, halves y on the curve.

pick.q: What does the graph of y = kx (k > 0) look like?
pick.r: A straight line through the origin
w: A curve that never meets the axes
A straight line that does not pass through the origin
A U-shaped curve
e: That is y = k ÷ x.
When x = 0, y = k × 0 = 0: the line passes through the origin.
That is y = kx².
pick.y: y = kx is a straight line; x = 0 gives y = 0.

pick.q: What does the graph of y = k ÷ x (k > 0, x > 0) look like?
pick.r: A curve that gets closer to both axes but never meets them
w: A straight line through the origin
A U-shaped curve through the origin
A straight line sloping down to the x-axis
e: That is direct variation, y = kx.
That is y = kx².
y = k ÷ x is never zero, so it never reaches the x-axis.
pick.y: y = k ÷ x: as x grows, y shrinks towards zero but never reaches it.

pick.q: What does the graph of y = kx² (k > 0) look like?
pick.r: A U-shaped curve (parabola) through the origin
w: A straight line through the origin
A curve that never meets the axes
A straight line that does not pass through the origin
e: y doubles when x doubles only for y = kx; here y is four times as big.
That is y = k ÷ x.
x = 0 gives y = 0: it passes through the origin.
pick.y: y = kx² is a parabola with its lowest point at the origin.

pick.q: z varies jointly as x and y. Which formula is right?
w: z = k(x + y)
z = kx ÷ y
z = xy
e: Jointly means multiply, not add.
kx ÷ y means inversely as y.
There must be a constant k.

pick.q: z varies directly as x and inversely as y. Which formula is right?
w: z = kxy
z = ky ÷ x
z = k(x − y)
e: That is jointly as x and y.
x and y are the wrong way round.
Variation uses multiplying or dividing.
pick.y: Directly as x (top), inversely as y (bottom).

pick.q: P varies directly as the square of v and inversely as r. Which formula is right?
w: P = kvr²
P = kr ÷ v²
P = k(v² − r)
e: r should divide, not multiply.
v² goes on top, r at the bottom.
Variation uses multiplying and dividing.

questions.prompt: z varies jointly as x and y, and z = {k * x * y} when x = {x} and y = {y}. Find k.

misconceptions.explain: Divide by both x and y: {x} × {y} = {x * y}.

solution: z = kxy: {k * x * y} = k × {x * y}.

questions.prompt: z varies directly as x and inversely as y. z = {k * x / y} when x = {x} and y = {y}. Find z when x = {X} and y = {Y}.

misconceptions.explain: x is on top (direct) and y at the bottom (inverse): z = {k} × {X} ÷ {Y}.

solution: z = kx ÷ y: {k * x / y} = k × {x} ÷ {y}, so k = {k}.
where: k * Y / X != k * X / Y

questions.prompt: y varies directly as x². By what number is y multiplied when x is multiplied by {n}?

misconceptions.explain: y varies as the square: ({n})² = {n * n}, not {n}.

solution: y = kx². Replace x by {n}x: y = k({n}x)² = {n * n}kx².
